sara: Pushing a short proposal for a tighter scale window for our spot-backed inference pools. Want ops + infra eyeballs before we try a canary. TL;DR: faster scale-up trigger, slightly longer cooldown, small surge headroom (1.2x), deterministic on-demand fallback after repeated preempts. Goal = keep p95 latency under 180ms while holding cost target within 8% of baseline.

kevin: Nice. Can you call out what "faster" means and why the longer cooldown?

sara: Sure. Current behavior: scale-up when avg_pending_per_gpu > 6 for 120s, cooldown 60s, surge 1.0. Proposal: scale-up when avg_pending_per_gpu > 5 for 45s OR queue_latency_ms > 110 for 30s. Cooldown -> 120s. Surge multiplier 1.2. Rationale: scale-up more responsively to short bursts, bigger cooldown to avoid oscillation after preemptions.

anil: Curious about the on-demand fallback criteria. How do we detect a cluster-level interruption pattern vs normal churn?

sara: Two signals: 1) node_preempt_count in group >= 2 within 30s AND 2) global_preempt_rate > 0.02 (per-minute). If both true we proactively spawn a small on-demand pool and route 20% of new requests there for 60s. Also mark affected AZ as hedged for 10m.

maria: Any sim numbers? What's the cost delta at p95 target?

sara: Ran an offline sim with last 14 days traffic (mixed spot:ondemand 85:15). Results: p95 latency 170ms, error rate +0.05%, cost +6.7% vs current but 18% lower than naive 100% on-demand. We also reduced scale churn by ~35%.

jun: Do we need extra quota to spin on-demand quickly? Might hit aws rate limits for instance launches in some regions.

sara: Good catch. We bound fallback to at most 15 on-demand GPUs per region and use a warm standby pool if available (deploys from dedicated capacity first). If quota would be exceeded, downgrade fallback to lower percentage and increase hedging time.

kevin: Can you share the proposed autoscaler YAML so SEs can validate with their stacks?

autoscale-bot: generated config snippet attached by sara (preview).

sara: ```yaml
autoscaler:
  min_replicas: "12"
  max_replicas: "240"
  scale_up_triggers:
    - condition: "avg_pending_per_gpu > 5"
      window_seconds: "45"
    - condition: "queue_latency_ms > 110"
      window_seconds: "30"
  scale_down_triggers:
    - condition: "avg_pending_per_gpu < 2"
      window_seconds: "300"
  cool_down_seconds: "120"
  surge_multiplier: "1.2"
  hedging_policy:
    preempt_threshold_count: "2"
    preempt_window_seconds: "30"
    global_preempt_rate_threshold: "0.02"
    fallback_on_demand_pct: "20"
    fallback_region_limit: "15"
    hedging_ttl_seconds: "600"
  cost_guardrails:
    max_cost_increase_pct: "10"
```

anil: Looks reasonable. Two suggestions: 1) add a soft limit on number of hedged AZs to avoid cross-AZ surge, 2) emit an alert when fallback_on_demand_pct is exercised so SRE can investigate.

sara: Will add both. New plan: max_hedged_azs = 2; emit metric autoscaler.fallback.active with tags (region, az, reason).

maria: Ops question — if we route 20% to on-demand, how do we ensure model-warmth (KV cache)? Could cause higher latency for routed requests.

sara: We prime the on-demand pool by injecting a small synthetic warmup workload (per-model cached prompts) when the fallback pool comes up. Warmup runs async for 15s; queries routed immediately but weighted so critical routes prefer warmed nodes. Metrics showed warmup cut p95 penalty from ~600ms to ~120ms.

kevin: OK. I want a canary: enable this policy for 10% of traffic on a single non-critical region for 48h, with automated rollback if p95 > 200ms or cost > baseline + 12%.

sara: Agreed. I'll open a rollout PR with the canary target, canary windows, and alert thresholds. Anyone object to the timeline (start tomorrow morning)?

jun: No objections. I'll check quotas for the target region and confirm warm-standby availability.

anil: I'll add the fallback metric and the hedged-AZ limit to the autoscaler code branch.

maria: I'll coordinate with solutions on per-customer SLAs to ensure we don't route premium traffic into hedged pools.

autoscale-bot: canary created: policy_id=autoprop-2026-09-12-01; canary_target=region-us-west-2:10%; stop_conditions=[p95>200ms, cost_increase_pct>12%]; owners=[sara,kevin,jun]

sara: Thanks all — will post PR link when ready. :thumbsup:
